title: A state import could install an haproxy.cfg that bypassed the global policy
description:
A node's haproxy.cfg is normally applied through HAProxyService.ApplyConfiguration, which runs the global policy (a chroot, uid/gid 1000, exactly janusd's stats socket, no second socket, no daemon/master-worker/program section). `SystemService.StateImport` staged a node's STATE straight onto disk, including haproxy/haproxy.cfg, and janusd applied it at its next start without that check, so an admin could durably install a configuration the policy forbids (no uid/chroot, or a second stats socket).

**Affected**: a node an os:admin can reach, with `-manage-host` (a real node).

**Fix**: the import checks the haproxy.cfg against the node's global policy before it is staged and rejects the whole import if it fails; off a managed node (native janusd) there is no policy and no check.

**Besides updating**: nothing.
